kb_proposals: A local isometry descends along a surjective local isometry (IsLocalIsometry.of_comp_right) and cancels an isometric embedding on the left (of_comp_left): with these, a map out of a quotient or into an open subset is checked on the cover / on the ambient space.

In a proof about a developing pair, never `set q := UniversalCover.proj M x₀`: `set` rewrites the type of ρ : Deck (proj …) →* isom d into a shadowing copy, and hypotheses about the old ρ stop matching (`ρ✝ γ = ρ γ`).
The deck group of the ported universal cover is transitive on fibres: leftMul by cb·ca⁻¹ (UniversalCover.exists_deck_apply_eq).

A local isometry out of Γ\𝐌ⁿ is onto: lift to Ñ (mathlib existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts; 𝐌ⁿ and convex Ω are SimplyConnectedSpace via Convex.contractibleSpace), compose with 𝒟_N, rigidity (developing_unique_of_preconnected with D := Subtype.val) gives g, and range F = {z | F(g⁻¹•𝒟 z) = z} is closed (Ñ T2, t2Space_universalCover) and open.

The end of a lifting argument for a convex domain: if F : Ω → Ñ lifts f ∘ π with 𝒟 ∘ F = g|Ω and range 𝒟 ⊆ gΩ, then σ := F ∘ g⁻¹ ∘ 𝒟 is defined on all of Ñ and range F = {σ z = z} is clopen (Classification.surjective_of_lift_of_range_subset); equivariance of the lift comes free from uniqueness of lifts + transitivity of the deck group on fibres + Causal.eq_of_eqOn (exists_deck_of_lift).

findings: Impossible in family (b), not in general. The pair-with-swap configuration (L(Γ) elementary, preserving a pair of null directions u₁ ≠ u₂ and exchanging them, no global fixed point) is impossible for a Cauchy-compact GH spacetime of family (b): centrality (L(γ)|_E = id, hEcen) makes the swap σ fix E pointwise, false_of_swap_fix_perp (det −1) then forces E ≠ P^⊥, and that yields the obstruction f ∈ P^⊥, f ⊥ E (hfE). The Lean theorem is exactly this family-(b) statement (hB : IsCHCentralExtensionOf B Γ). Example of a non-compact instance under centrality, 𝐌³ (d = 2): Γ = ⟨γ₀, σ⟩, γ₀ = boost along x composed with the translation ∂_y, σ the half-turn (t,x,y) ↦ (t,−x,−y); σγ₀σ⁻¹ = γ₀⁻¹ (infinite dihedral), E = 0, L(Γ) without global fixed point, and the Cauchy surface (ℝ²/⟨(a,1)⟩)/σ is not compact. This is the infinite-dihedral group of G9's own Finding; it never occurs in family (b) under Cauchy-compactness.

Outside family (b) the configuration exists, and Barbot covers it; no defect in the paper. Cauchy-compact example, 𝐌⁴ (d = 3), q = 2xy + z₁² + z₂², Ω = {x>0, y<0} × ℝ² (Misner): Γ' = {(x,z,y) ↦ (eᵏx, z+w, e⁻ᵏy) : k ∈ ℤ, w ∈ 2u₁ℤ ⊕ ℤ}, u₁ ≠ 0; σ(x,z₁,z₂,y) = (−y, z₁+u₁, −z₂, −x) has det +1, preserves time orientation and Ω, σ² ∈ Γ' and σΓ'σ⁻¹ = Γ'. Γ = ⟨Γ', σ⟩ acts freely (the z₁-coordinate of any σg moves by u₁ + 2u₁ℤ ∌ 0) and properly, the Cauchy surface ({xy = −1} × ℝ²)/Γ is compact, L(Γ) = ⟨boost, swap⟩ is discrete with no global fixed point, Λ(Γ) lies over {u₁, u₂}. It is a finite quotient of a Misner spacetime and is not of family (b): E = P^⊥ and L(σ)|_E = diag(1,−1) ≠ id. Barbot treats it: [10.M] opens 'Here, we consider the case where, up to finite index, $L(\Gamma)$ preserves some isotropic direction $\Delta_{0}$' (l.3237–3239), which reaches the swap through the index-2 subgroup, and Theorem B is stated 'Up to finite coverings' (l.355).
